name: pfd-deadzone (operating point)
description: residual charge offset of the PFD + charge pump, and the static phase offset that nulls it, across DR-001 Decision 2's ratified control window at the closed loop's own reference frequency
claim: #394 -- `spec/pll.md` cites this campaign's `t_offset` (0.671 ns at `ff`/125 C/3.63 V) as the SYSTEMATIC term of its static phase-offset budget, but that number is measured at f_ref = 25 MHz with the control node pinned at 1.65 V, while `sim/supply-sensitivity` measured 1.796 ns of static REF->FB phase at the same PVT corner running at f_ref = 12.5 MHz with the loop's control node near 2.29 V. Is the 2.7x gap the operating point? This manifest measures the identical quantity, on the identical DUT, at the closed loop's own reference frequency and across the whole ratified 0.9-2.4 V control window, so the operating-point dependence is measured rather than argued.
methodology: **Same DUT, same measurement, different operating point.** The DUT (`pfd_cp`), the stimulus topology, the ideal bias references, the 200 ps edges, the Icp trim code (b1 b0 = 10, 3 unit legs) and every solver option are `testbench/tb.json`'s, unchanged. Exactly three things differ, and they are the variables #394 asks about: `period` is 80 ns (12.5 MHz) instead of 40 ns; `vctrl` is a declared sweep axis over 0.90 / 1.65 / 2.40 V instead of one point at 1.65 V; and the charge-integration window is expressed relative to `period` instead of as a literal. Per sim/README.md ('Two manifests, one experiment directory') this stays in the `pfd-deadzone` directory rather than becoming a sibling slug, because it is the same DUT measured a second way.

**The reported quantity is `t_offset` = -q_zero / kd_wide**, the static phase offset at the PFD inputs that nulls the pump's residual per-cycle charge -- the same reduction `testbench/derive.py` computes, so the two records' numbers are directly comparable. `q_zero` is the net charge delivered per reference cycle at dphi = 0 and `kd_wide = [q(+1ns) - q(-1ns)] / 2ns` is the detector gain well outside the reset window.

**The dphi axis is the wide pair plus zero, and nothing else.** The near pair (+/-200 ps) exists in the parent manifest to test LINEARITY through zero -- the dead-zone claim. That claim is the parent's and is already answered (45/45 corners pass, worst ratio 1.13); re-testing it at a second operating point is not this record's question, and the three points here are exactly what `t_offset` needs. No dead-zone verdict is computed or claimed by this manifest.

**f_ref = 12.5 MHz is not a weaker choice than the parent's 25 MHz -- it is a different one.** 25 MHz is the TOP of DR-002 Decision 1's ratified 1-25 MHz range, where the PFD's reset-and-recover window is the largest fraction of the reference period, and it is the demanding end for a dead-zone claim. 12.5 MHz is the reference `sim/supply-sensitivity`'s closed loop actually runs at (100 MHz / N = 8), which is the only reason it appears here. A `t_offset` difference between the two manifests at the same corner and the same 1.65 V is therefore a measurement of the f_ref dependence, with every other variable held.

**The control-window ladder is DR-001 Decision 2's own window, not a convenience triple.** 0.90 V and 2.40 V are the stated ends of the ~0.9-2.4 V usable control window (the same bounds `sim/supply-sensitivity`'s `ACC_VCTRL_LO`/`ACC_VCTRL_HI` apply to its closed-loop rows); 1.65 V is its middle and the parent manifest's single point, retained here so the f_ref comparison above has a held-constant control voltage to run through.

**The charge-integration window is period-relative** -- `from='tstart+period' to='tstart+3*period'` rather than the parent's literal `from=60n to=140n`. It integrates the same two whole reference cycles (the 2nd and the 3rd; the 1st is discarded as PFD start-up, both latches powering up reset) at either period, and reproduces the parent's `qnet2` bit-for-bit (-6.99339e-15 C) at the parent's own 40 ns / 1.65 V / `ff`/125 C/3.63 V settings.

Transient: 3 reference cycles at 80 ns = 240 ns of signal, run to 280 ns, 20 ps maximum timestep, `reltol` 1e-4 / `abstol` 1e-14 -- the parent manifest's controls, with only the stop time extended to cover the longer period.

`rshunt = 1e12` is set for the parent manifest's reason: a disabled trim leg's cascode mid-node is driven only by two off devices and is floating for the DC solution; the shunt contributes 3.3 pA at 3.3 V, below the abstol floor. `itl4 = 200` raises the transient Newton-iteration limit -- a solver-EFFORT knob, not a tolerance, so the converged solution is unchanged.

**Limitation (open loop, and that is the point)**: the control node is held by an ideal source, so this measures the charge the pump delivers and NOT what a real loop filter does with it. A closed-loop static phase offset that exceeds `t_offset` at the loop's own operating point is therefore evidence that something other than the pump's residual charge is setting it -- which is precisely the inference #394 needs, and why the open-loop isolation is retained rather than relaxed.

**Limitation (nominal skew only)**: `sw_stat_global = sw_stat_mismatch = 0`. Random device mismatch on the charge pump is #15's campaign (`mc-cp-mismatch`); every `t_offset` here is the SYSTEMATIC residue, which is the term `spec/pll.md`'s budget names.

**Axes not swept**: passive corner sections (`res_*`, `mimcap_*`, `moscap_*`) N/A -- the DUT contains no resistors or capacitors, only `nfet_03v3`/`pfet_03v3` (DR-002 Decision 3). The 2-bit Icp trim is held at the nominal b1 b0 = 10 for the parent manifest's reason, and because it is the code `sim/supply-sensitivity` runs its closed loop at; trim range across corners is `cp-compliance`'s campaign.

vc.description: control-node voltage -- DR-001 Decision 2's ratified ~0.9-2.4 V window, at its two ends and its middle. 1.65 V is the parent manifest's single point and is what makes the f_ref comparison against it a one-variable comparison.

v0p90.description: 0.90 V -- the bottom of the ratified control window

v1p65.description: 1.65 V -- the middle, and the parent manifest's only control point

v2p40.description: 2.40 V -- the top of the ratified control window; the `ff`/125 C/3.63 V closed loop settles at 2.29 V, just inside it

d.description: dphi -- FB-relative-to-REF phase offset. Zero gives the residual charge q_zero; the +/-1 ns pair gives the detector gain kd_wide that converts it to a phase. The parent manifest's near pair (+/-200 ps) is a linearity probe for its dead-zone verdict and is deliberately absent here.

d-1n.description: FB 1 ns early -- the gain pair's negative end

d0.description: zero phase error -- where the residual charge q_zero is read

d1n.description: FB 1 ns late -- the gain pair's positive end

width_up.expr: trig v(up) val='vdd_val/2' rise=3 targ v(up) val='vdd_val/2' fall=3

width_dn.expr: trig v(dn) val='vdd_val/2' rise=3 targ v(dn) val='vdd_val/2' fall=3

phase-to-charge transfer.description: net charge delivered per reference cycle at this (control voltage, phase offset) point, and the UP/DN pulse widths behind it

residual at dphi = 0.description: the residual charge the loop must null as static phase error; measured only at the dphi = 0 points, `not measured` everywhere else by construction. The phase it corresponds to divides by a gain differenced across two dphi points, so it is per (corner, control voltage) in pfd_static_offset.csv
